title: SO-2.05 Cross-functional issue discovery without unrestricted access to private records
request: Closes G-SO-16. Source: the master traceability baseline of 31 October 2026 (section 8.3) and, where named, the Scope One addendum (PR #222, docs/scope-one/ADDENDUM-ARCHITECTURE-AND-DELIVERY-REVIEW.md at head a1757a0); 8.3 to 8.6 released for contracting by the owner on 31 Oct 2026. This contract is the design-record stage: it asks for the decision record and builds nothing. Contracts marked with a dagger are signed in the owner's vault and are not visible in this repository. The programme decomposition on branch docs/engine-decision-tiers-reconcile (docs/scope-one/programme/) is read for overlap: WP08-04 and WP14-04 are prototype and demonstrator tasks; this contract is the design record for the routing and access rules and takes neither.

tasks.title: Decision record
requirements: Surface relevant information between departments without granting unrestricted access to their private records

Let an authorised person or agent discover relevant work elsewhere in the organisation. For example, an agent assisting with a new customer proposal could discover a delivery constraint identified by engineering, a contractual commitment recorded by operations, a pricing assumption from finance, or a previous customer issue that materially changes the proposal.

Support both explicit retrieval and proactive discovery. Agents should be able to query the relevant organisational context, while background analysis may surface material cross-project relationships, anomalies, risks and opportunities for review.

Route consequential findings into the appropriate owner or decision workflow. Do not silently edit approved project scope, alter commitments, disclose restricted information or change business policy.
